items.title: California warns of measles exposure in six counties from unvaccinated train passenger
items.author: Marina Dunbar
items.content:
Health authorities work to notify people who were exposed to person who traveled through at least six counties

California public health officials are warning of a possible measles exposure spanning multiple counties after an infected and unvaccinated passenger traveled through the state via Amtrak trains and thruway buses.

The warning comes as the US faces its largest measles resurgence in more than three decades, fueled largely by growing vaccine hesitancy.

Continue reading...

items.title: Manchester United Muslim fans group calls on co-owner Jim Ratcliffe to quit
items.author: Yassin El-Moudden and Daniel Lavelle
items.content:
Supporters’ club says billionaire should stand down after ‘completely unacceptable’ comments on the UK and empire

Manchester United’s Muslim supporters’ Club (MUMSC) has called for the Premier League side’s co-owner to step down after he made “completely unacceptable” comments during a BBC interview.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe described the UK as being a country “on the slide” from the days when it had “the greatest empire in the world”.

Continue reading...

items.title: Newsom Signs Bills Meant to Prevent Trump’s Interference in Midterms
items.author: Laurel Rosenhall
items.content: <article>Gov. Gavin Newsom of California signed legislation that would make it illegal to interfere with ballots or election records in response to efforts by the president to restrict voting.</article>

items.title: Kent hotel fire that forced hundreds to evacuate being treated as suspicious
items.author: Sammy Gecsoyler and Yassin El-Moudden
items.content:
No injuries reported after about 280 people taken to safety from the Grand Burstin in Folkestone after blaze

A large fire that broke out overnight at a seaside hotel and forced hundreds of people to evacuate is being treated by police as suspicious.

Emergency services were called just after 1am on Saturday to the Grand Burstin hotel in Folkestone, where a fire is believed to have started in the basement, Kent fire and rescue service said.

Continue reading...

items.title: Creating a Kill Switch to Shut Down a Rogue A.I. Is Harder Than It Sounds
items.author: Dylan Freedman and Dustin Volz
items.content: <article>A bipartisan group in Congress and Gov. Gavin Newsom of California have floated ideas for building a mechanism that would instantly power down an A.I. system. Only no one really knows how.</article>

items.title: Lindsay Clancy ex-husband says ‘I think I did the best I could’
items.author: Edward Helmore
items.content:
Patrick Clancy and wife Rachel Danis to speak publicly on 60 Minutes on Sunday about Massachusetts murder trial

Patrick Clancy and his wife Rachel Danis are set to describe their experiences of the Massachusetts triple-murder trial of his former wife Lindsay Clancy, with Clancy telling 60 Minutes: “I live with it every day, but I think I did the best I could.”

The couple will on Sunday night make their first public comments on the case. CBS has been trailing excerpts of the broadcast.

Continue reading...

items.title: Elderly man allegedly beaten to death in Virginia Walmart by parents of employee
items.author: Marina Dunbar
items.content:
Bert Atienza and teen worker reportedly exchanged words before parents showed up and allegedly attacked shopper

A 77-year-old Walmart shopper died after he was allegedly attacked inside a Virginia store by the parents of a teenage employee he had confronted over a shopping cart incident involving his wife, according to US media reports.

Bert Atienza died from blunt head trauma on 8 June, one day after the attack at the Walmart in Norfolk, Virginia, WTKR reported on Monday. The shocking incident was captured on surveillance video.

Continue reading...

items.title: Thick smoke seen near Riyadh airport after air raid alerts in Saudi capital
items.author: Donna Ferguson, Yassin El-Moudden and agencies
items.content:
Authorities also issued warnings for Jeddah and Yanbu, a major industrial port and home to vital oil facilities

Flames and a large plume of black smoke were seen rising above Riyadh airport in Saudi Arabia on Saturday after the government sent air raid alerts to citizens by phone overnight warning of aerial attacks.

Explosions were heard in the capital as firefighters battled to extinguish the flames of a burning fuel tank emblazoned with the logo of the Saudi oil company Aramco near the city’s King Khalid international airport.

Continue reading...

items.title: George Osborne ‘thought Peter Thiel’s Bayeux tapestry visit would be secret’
items.author: Helena Horton and Nadia Khomami
items.content:
British Museum chair tells Big Brue festival he thought no one would find out about the private viewing

George Osborne has said he thought no one would find out about a private viewing of the Bayeux tapestry he organised for the tech billionaire Peter Thiel at the British Museum.

The former chancellor, who is chair of the museum, told the Big Brue festival in Somerset that he had been on holiday when Thiel was shown the medieval artwork.

Continue reading...

items.title: At DraftKings, AI Targets the Gamblers Likeliest to Lose
items.author: Alex Klavens, Walt Bogdanich and Jenny Vrentas
items.content: <article>Data science helps determine who receives betting incentives, but the company has resisted using similar technology to protect gamblers at risk of addiction.</article>

items.title: MS Now, CNN and Politico say reporters have been denied access to White House
items.author: Edward Helmore
items.content:
President said he was banning journalists from those organizations, saying of their coverage: ‘You get sick of it.’

Journalists from three US outlets were denied access to the White House grounds on Saturday morning a day after Donald Trump said he would ban them from the executive branch complex in a move that has prompted outrage and shock from free speech advocates.

The outlets were television broadcasters MS now and CNN as well as the political news website Politico.

Continue reading...

items.title: Jewish heirs of Holocaust victims sue California museum over Nazi-looted art
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
Pasadena’s Norton Simon Museum holds 16th-century paintings stolen by the Nazis during the second world war

Jewish heirs of Holocaust victims and their representatives have filed two lawsuits in California staking their claims to Nazi-looted paintings that still hang on the walls of prominent museums in Los Angeles and Auschwitz.

This pair of lawsuits are the first to be filed after the recent passage of laws by California and the US Congress, which strengthen US-based claims to artwork that were forcibly taken from Jewish families during the second world war.

Continue reading...

items.title: Trump’s battle to rename the Kennedy Center has put its future at risk
items.author: David Smith in Washington
items.content:
The president has threatened to block renovations and suggested the landmark could be demolished after courts ruled against his bid to rename it

It was born with the world premiere of Leonard Bernstein’s Mass. “Young people will come here and they will see this cultural centre,” Rose Kennedy, the mother of slain US president John F Kennedy, said at that opening night gala. “They will carry some of these ideas back to their different communities.”

More than half a century later, the potential death knell came just after 4.30pm on Tuesday with a perfunctory announcement on the public address system: “The centre is now closed to the public. Please exit the centre by way of the Hall of States.” Soon barricades had been erected and security guards were blocking access.

Continue reading...

items.title: ‘Nervous and Skeptical,’ Greenlanders Question the New Deal With Trump
items.author: Jeffrey Gettleman and Maya Tekeli
items.content: <article>The U.S. president’s threats to seize Greenland left its people on edge, and with details scarce, the news of an agreement didn’t seem to be putting minds at ease.</article>

items.title: Scottish Labour’s new leader backs Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gasfields
items.author: Patrick Greenfield
items.content:
Michael Marra supports development of the North Sea sites, calling for a ‘more rational’ approach to energy policy

Scottish Labour’s new leader Michael Marra has backed the development of the Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gasfields in the North Sea in one of his first acts after being elected, calling for a “more rational” approach to energy policy.

On Saturday, the MSP for North East Scotland won a near two-thirds majority to lead the party in Holyrood, becoming Scottish Labour’s 11th leader. He replaces Anas Sarwar after his shock decision to resign in July to join Andy Burnham’s new government as a trade minister.

Continue reading...

items.title: Behold the Most Handsome Melons in Mexico
items.author: James Wagner and Luis Antonio Rojas
items.content: <article>In the eastern city of Xalapa, what started as a joke among friends over two decades ago has become a vibrant annual tradition that highlights creativity and absurdity with melons.</article>

items.title: Aaron Sorkin Goes Off Script
items.author: Lulu Garcia-Navarro
items.content: <article>The Oscar-winning writer returns to Facebook with “The Social Reckoning”— and surprises us with the revelation of why he is so drawn to uplift and romance. </article>

items.title: Trump’s Security Deal With Greenland: What to Know
items.author: Maya Tekeli, Lynsey Chutel and Amelia Nierenberg
items.content: <article>President Trump insisted for months that the Danish territory should be part of the United States. Now, a security deal — not a takeover — seems to be on the table.</article>

items.title: Has Trump Lost Touch With Reality?
items.author: Michelle Cottle, David French, Michelle Goldberg and Jillian Weinberger
items.content: <article>Three Opinions writers debate whether the president’s recent behavior is really that different from what we’ve seen from him over the years.</article>

items.title: Inside the Breakdown of U.K.-Israel Relations Over West Bank Settlements
items.author: Aaron Boxerman, Adam Rasgon and Stephen Castle
items.content: <article>British officials believed Israel had said it would hold off on moving ahead with construction in E1, a piece of land viewed as vital to a future Palestinian state. Israel said it promised no such thing.</article>

items.title: Trump and Xi Can Make Progress on A.I.
items.author: Nicholas Kristof
items.content: <article>Xi is in the driver’s seat, reflecting American weakness, but there still may be some space for limited advances.</article>

items.title: Students scramble for accommodation after provider goes bust in Dundee
items.author: Julia Kollewe and Amee Joshi
items.content:
Case highlights severe financial strain on sector across UK as string of university housing schemes fail

Nearly 70 students in Dundee have been left scrambling to find accommodation for this academic year after the latest in a string of university housing schemes went bust amid severe financial strain on the sector.

Students in the city have been forced to find alternative housing and rapidly move their possessions as term begins this month after the collapse of the owner of Marketgait Apartments, a city centre block.

Continue reading...

items.title: Fading Light
items.author: Melissa Kirsch
items.content: <article>Fall officially begins on Tuesday, but evidence of the season seeps in more gradually.</article>

items.title: Record fuel prices across EU prompt calls for bloc-wide windfall tax on firms
items.author: Jon Henley Europe correspondent and Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
items.content:
German minister says companies are ‘exploiting situation’ in Middle East, as sky-high prices become major domestic issue for leaders

European governments have discussed imposing a bloc-wide windfall tax on energy companies, as near-record fuel and gas prices pile pressure on leaders desperate to contain mounting public discontent and the challenge of the far right.

With elections due next year in eight EU countries including France, Italy, Spain and Poland, leaders are scrambling to head off the potential fallout from what analysts have warned could be one of the continent’s biggest energy shocks in decades.

Continue reading...

items.title: Shark catch-and-kill order issued after swimmer dies off popular Perth beach
items.author: Achol Arok and Kat Wong
items.content:
Man, 63, fatally bitten by shark at Sorrento beach on Friday morning

A shark that fatally attacked a man on a beach in Perth’s north will be “destroyed” if it is captured, after an order was issued by the Western Australian government.

As the hunt for the animal remained under way on Saturday, the WA fisheries minister, Jackie Jarvis, revealed she had greenlit the order.

Continue reading...

items.title: From ovations in Venice to death threats in Israel: the extreme responses to NAZA documentary
items.author: Peter Beaumont
items.content:
As Gaza documentary wins cinematic acclaim, its directors face vitriol in Israel amid a febrile election campaign

First there was a moment of stunned silence. Then, in the Sala Grande, the main screening hall of the Venice film festival within the Palazzo del Cinema, the audience stood almost as one and turned to applaud the film-makers for 25 minutes.

The film the audience had watched for 80 harrowing minutes was the Gaza documentary NAZA, which has been produced by the Guardian.

Continue reading...

items.title: ‘My fear was too great’: the Pussy Riot member recruited by Russian spies to inform on fellow activists
items.author: Shaun Walker
items.content:
Exclusive: In her first media interview since fleeing Russia, Rita Flores describes her three years of being run by the FSB

First came the blackmail and death threats to secure cooperation, then came a series of tasks, each more sinister than the last: to inform on fellow activists, to elicit personal information from protest-minded artists and – eventually – to help with a plot to kidnap and murder a Kremlin enemy.

That is how Rita Flores, a 29-year-old Russian artist, activist and former member of the Pussy Riot collective, described her recruitment and three-year handling by officers from Russia’s FSB security service, a cooperation she only broke when she fled the country last month.

Continue reading...

items.title: US and Denmark reach security deal after Trump’s threats to take over Greenland
items.author: Robert Mackey
items.content:
The agreement would allow the US to expand its military presence, while Denmark and Greenland say it preserves their sovereignty and right to self-determination

Donald Trump announced on Friday that the US had struck an Arctic security pact with the leaders of Denmark and Greenland, after threatening for much of his second term to annex the semi-autonomous Danish territory by force.

The full scope of the deal Trump described as “very important, historic, and special” was not immediately clear. But soon after his announcement in a post on Truth Social, the leaders of Denmark and Greenland issued statements indicating the deal would be signed by the three governments on the sidelines of the United Nations general assembly in New York City next week.

Continue reading...

items.title: Men deported from US bound and beaten in Equatorial Guinea detention hotel, lawyers say
items.author: Maanvi Singh
items.content:
Group trapped at Hotel Bamy after US removal as rights groups sound alarm over poor conditions and violence

Two men that the Trump administration expelled to Equatorial Guinea were bound, fitted with bags over their heads, beaten and pushed down a flight of stairs, all in plain view of other US deportees, according to witnesses and human rights lawyers.

The men – one from Egypt and one from Eritrea – were then taken to a prison. About 30 detainees from the US remain trapped at a hotel in the outskirts of the coastal city of Malabo after being deported from the US. Detainees have said they believe the men were beaten for telling the press and human rights advocates about the poor conditions and violence inside the hotel, and that they are haunted by flashbacks and terrified they will be retaliated against next.

Continue reading...

items.title: Latvia’s president warns that Europe is not up to date with drone and aerial warfare in Ukraine
items.author: Andrew Roth in Washington
items.content:
Edgars Rinkēvičs says drone warfare in Ukraine is moving at ‘lightning speed’ and efforts to prepare for an aerial war could be obsolete by next year

Latvia’s president has warned that Europe is not keeping up with developments of drone and aerial warfare in Ukraine and that most countries in Nato could not repulse an attack by Russian missiles if the conflict expands.

The remarks came during a Guardian interview in Washington DC in which Edgars Rinkēvičs said that the technological developments in drone warfare in Ukraine are moving at “lightning speed” and that current efforts to prepare for an aerial war could be obsolete by the middle of next year.

Continue reading...

items.title: A.G. Sulzberger: The Story of America, Told in 15 Million First Drafts of History
items.author: A.G. Sulzberger
items.content: <article>The Times has witnessed the country’s transformation. It will keep its eyes open.</article>

items.title: Survivors recount panic and struggle to breathe in Nigerian prison cell where 37 died
items.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan and agencies
items.content:
Police fire teargas as protests break out in city of Minna after deaths of suspected illegal goldminers, many of whom were children

Survivors from a prison cell in Nigeria where 37 suspected illegal goldminers died while in the custody of a paramilitary group this week have recounted their panic and struggle for breath, as police on Friday fired teargas at people protesting against the deaths and imposed an overnight curfew in the city of Minna.

The victims – many of whom were children – were found dead on Thursday in the cells of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), which had raided suspected illegal goldmines and ⁠locked up dozens of miners in the city, the state capital of the mineral-rich state of Niger.

Continue reading...

items.title: Brazil’s Lula announces higher welfare payments and free weight-loss jabs ahead of election
items.author: Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
items.content:
Critics say moves from leftwing incumbent president are electorally motivated two weeks before Brazil’s elections

Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has announced a 15% increase in the country’s main cash-transfer programme for poor families, as well as free weight-loss jabs, prompting criticism from opponents who say the moves are electorally motivated just two weeks before the presidential election.

On 4 October, the leftwing incumbent will face the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who has been gaining ground in recent weeks.

Continue reading...

items.title: Alleged underworld supporters and unfounded health claims: One Nation rolls out more Victorian election candidates
items.author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
items.content:
Party has unveiled a steady stream of contenders for state election, including a former councillor who lost his licence for drink-driving

Candidates contesting the Victorian state election for One Nation include a former Liberal who has won support from alleged underworld figures, a naturopath who has endorsed Donald Trump’s unfounded claim that paracetamol is linked to autism and a former shire councillor who lost his licence for drink-driving.

Pauline Hanson announced who would be her party’s upper house candidates and Victorian leader, Warren Pickering, at a press conference last month. Since then One Nation has used social media to unveil a steady stream of candidates, with 51 of the 88 lower house spots now filled.

Continue reading...

items.title: Swedish teenager jailed for attempted murder, rape and assault committed online, with victims in Germany and Australia
items.author: Ariel Bogle
items.content:
Eighteen-year-old known as Chai was active in networks notorious for their sadistic exploitation of young people

The district court found that Chai, 18, was active in online networks notorious for their sadistic extortion of young and vulnerable people, coercing them to create sexually explicit material or engage in acts of violence – and for the youth of those involved.

Continue reading...

items.title: Yemen’s anti-Houthi forces launch inquest into sudden military collapse
items.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
items.content:
Rout raises questions about coordination and morale as some politicians claim billions of dollars were offered to persuade forces to abandon position

A bitter inquest is under way among Yemen’s anti-Houthi forces as to how what was being billed as a decisive assault on Sana’a, the Houthi-controlled capital, suddenly collapsed into a military rout.

More than 15 brigades were defeated as the country’s entire west coast fell into Houthi hands. Efforts are now being made to reorganise the anti-Houthi forces representing the UN-recognised Yemeni government in order to capture the Kahbob mountains, a strategic point from which to restrict Houthi forces moving closer to the crucial Bab al-Mandab strait.

Continue reading...

items.title: British Sikh man granted bail in India nine years after arrest
items.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
items.content:
Jagtar Singh Johal, from Scotland, was arrested after wedding in Punjab on alleged terrorism offences

Jagtar Singh Johal, a British Sikh man who was arrested in India in 2017 in connection with alleged terrorism offences, has been granted bail by a Delhi court.

Johal, from Scotland, was arrested for his alleged role in funding the Khalistan Liberation Force, which had carried out targeted killings in India’s Punjab region.

Continue reading...

items.title: British woman who was kidnapped in Malawi rescued by police after shootout
items.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
items.content:
Four of Nurat Osman’s alleged abductors were killed during rescue after she was taken from outside her home last week

A British woman kidnapped in Malawi last week has been rescued by police after a shootout in which four of her alleged abductors were killed.

Nusrat Osman was abducted outside her home in the southern city of Blantyre on 11 September at about 12.30pm. Police had offered a reward of 30m Malawi kwacha (£12,950) for information leading to her rescue and the arrest of the perpetrators.

Continue reading...

items.title: Australian man accused of murdering Thai teenager and putting body in suitcase pleads not guilty
items.author: Agence France-Presse and Associated Press
items.content:
Simon Peter Carman appeared in a Pattaya court on Friday charged with killing Tunchanok Donhomla

An Australian man accused of murdering a Thai teenager and putting her body in a suitcase pleaded not guilty on Friday in a hearing in the seaside resort city of Pattaya, a court official said.

Simon Peter Carman, 45, was arrested in June after 17-year-old Tunchanok Donhomla was reported missing in Pattaya City, about 150km south-east of Bangkok. A suitcase containing her body was found shortly after.

Continue reading...

items.title: Louisiana firefighters find feline native to sub-Saharan Africa while responding to house fire
items.author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
items.content:
The African serval, illegally enclosed in the back yard, was subdued and transferred to an animal welfare facility

Louisiana firefighters responding to a small house blaze found a wildcat native to sub-Saharan Africa illegally enclosed in the back yard, prompting an animal welfare agency to seek placing the creature in an appropriate environment, according to officials.

Firefighters investigating a report of a minor fire at a home in the suburban New Orleans community of Marrero on Tuesday spotted the cat in question – an African serval – behind the residence in a chain-linked enclosure resembling a cramped baseball batting cage, a spokesperson for the local animal protection services said.

Continue reading...

items.title: Iranian actor Laleh Marzban faces severe threats after Venice film festival speech
items.author: Philip Oltermann European culture editor
items.content:
Marzban, who won a best actress award for her portrayal of a woman held hostage by her father in Falling House, has received condemnations from authorities after dedicating her prize to ‘the women of Iran’

An Iranian actress who won the best newcomer award at the Venice film festival has come under severe attack from the country’s authorities and state media after highlighting the plight of women in Iran in her acceptance speech.

Laleh Marzban last Saturday won the best actress award in the Orizzonti sidebar competition for emerging talent, for her role in Mohsen Gharaei’s Falling House, a film revolving around three generations of women who are incarcerated in their own home by the family’s father.

Continue reading...

items.title: Andrew Hastie says AI advised him to reply ‘congratulations!’ to man who planned to end life with assisted dying
items.author: Luca Ittimani
items.content:
Liberal MP speaks of AI’s shortcomings as cyber chief tells inquiry the tech is needed to fend off ‘highly capable malicious cyber actors’

When a man with a terminal illness wrote to his local MP Andrew Hastie, telling him he planned on ending his own life with voluntary assisted dying, Microsoft Copilot suggested Hastie reply with “congratulations!”, “great to hear from you” or “that is wonderful news!”.

Hastie shared the episode at a parliamentary inquiry on Friday to underline the shortcomings of the American-run software as he called for AI run by Australians.

Continue reading...

items.title: Weather tracker: Thunderstorms hit Spain as Japan braces for typhoon
items.author: James Michelin for MetDesk
items.content:
At least one person dead as stormy weather causes severe flooding in Barcelona and Valencia

Intense and slow-moving thunderstorms broke out on Wednesday afternoon across parts of eastern Spain, bringing some severe flooding and killing at least one person.

Storms first struck over the Castilla-La Mancha region during the afternoon before passing over Spain’s east coast, becoming very slow-moving and continuing overnight. Torrential rainfall, strong winds and large hail were reported in Valencia and Barcelona, causing widespread flooding in both cities. Weather stations west of Barcelona recorded some of the highest totals with more than 100mm (4in) of rain falling in the space of a few hours, and locally 70mm in just 30 minutes in the early hours of Thursday morning. Cars and roads were submerged, and flights were cancelled across the region.

Continue reading...

items.title: ‘We have something that will kill Elliott’: Icac questions former Labor councillor over message
items.author: Penry Buckley
items.content:
Sharangan Maheswaran denies message he received about NSW minister was related to work for fugitive property developer

A former Labor councillor says he had a “common interest” with a conservative Liberal operative, but denied that a message he received about damaging the reputation of NSW Liberal minister David Elliott was related to political work for a fugitive property developer, an inquiry has heard.

Sharangan Maheswaran told the Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) on Friday that a message sent to him by lobbyist Jeremy Greenwood claiming “We have something that will kill Elliott” did not relate to work by Greenwood’s company Beckington for Jean Nassif.

Continue reading...

items.title: ‘We demand the truth’: Olga Tokarczuk and JM Coetzee lead calls for proof of life of disappeared Eritrean writers
items.author: Ella Creamer
items.content:
More than 180 writers sign letter renewing calls for information on 12 authors detained incommunicado since 2001 crackdown on free speech by Isaias Afwerki

More than 180 writers have signed a letter to Eritrean president Isaias Afwerki calling for proof of life for 12 writers arrested in 2001.

Nobel laureates Olga Tokarczuk and JM Coetzee join prominent writers including Colm Tóibín, Elif Shafak, Isabel Allende, Ben Okri, Yann Martel, Kamila Shamsie and Tsitsi Dangarembga in signing the letter organised by PEN International and dated 18 September, marking 25 years since a government crackdown on the independent press. “Within days, Eritrea’s free press and the nation’s independent voices were systematically crushed,” opens the letter.

Continue reading...

items.title: Japan raises interest rates to 31-year high to curb impact of rising prices
items.author: Mark Sweney and agencies
items.content:
Increase from 1% to 1.25% follows US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank tightening monetary policy

Japan’s central bank has increased interest rates to a fresh 31-year high as it attempts to combat global inflation linked to the war in Iran.

The Bank of Japan (BoJ) voted to raise its target interest rate from 1% to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995.

Continue reading...

items.title: South Korea will not send military to support US war on Iran, defying Trump pressure
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Seoul resolves recent speculation over sending military to strait of Hormuz, saying ‘there won’t be deployment that would involve or enter war’

South Korea’s president, Lee Jae Myung, has said he will ⁠not deploy the military to the ⁠Middle East in a way ​that could draw the country into conflict, resisting calls from Donald Trump to support his war in Iran.

“There won’t be deployment that would involve or enter war. I can tell you that very clearly,” Lee said at a ⁠news conference on Friday. “We won’t deploy military assets in any form to that end.”

Continue reading...

items.title: Indonesia gets its first aircraft carrier amid debate over cost and military ambitions
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
The gift from Italy has sparked fierce debate among defence analysts and opposition politicians who question its true cost and purpose

Indonesia has received its first aircraft carrier, a former Italian warship that the government says will strengthen the archipelagic nation’s maritime security and disaster response capabilities.

The 41-year-old former ITS Giuseppe Garibaldi, with capacity for short takeoff and vertical landing aircraft and helicopters, arrived Friday morning at a naval base in North Jakarta’s Tanjung Priok port, where it was welcomed with a military ceremony.

Continue reading...

items.title: Tell Us What Questions You Have About Winter Getaways and Holiday Travel
items.author: Deborah Dunn
items.content: <article>It isn’t too early to start thinking about end-of-year travel plans. We’re fielding reader questions about where to go and what to do.</article>

items.title: YouTube star Ms Rachel to match Macklemore’s $1m Palestine aid donation
items.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
items.content:
Educator talks of ‘moral obligation’ and urges ‘every wealthy white celebrity’ to make similar donation

Macklemore, who was fired as the opening act on Ed Sheeran’s tour after saying “Free Palestine” on stage at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium, pledged to donate the entirety of his earnings from Sheeran’s tour to several organizations focused on the Palestinian people.

Continue reading...

items.title: New cat species identified for first time in more than a century in Bolivia
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
New species of wild feline was discovered in Bolivia’s Yungas forest that is smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat

A diminutive wild cat that inhabits Bolivia’s ⁠cloud forest has been identified as a previously unknown species, marking the first time a new living feline species has been formally named and described in more than a century.

The cat, called tilcayo by local communities, is part of a group called tiger ⁠cats found across much of South ⁠America. It was found in Bolivia’s ​lush Yungas forest, a mountainous region where forests are often covered by clouds and surrounded by high humidity, according to researchers. It measures about 18in (46cm) long and weighs about 3lb (1.4kg), making it smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat.

Continue reading...

items.title: Share the Times Pages You Couldn’t Throw Away
items.author: The New York Times
items.content: <article>The New York Times has been publishing for 175 years. Some of that history may be sitting in a shoe box under your bed.</article>

items.title: All smiles in Strasbourg but uncertainty clouds Canada’s EU membership plan
items.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
items.content:
Although Mark Carney welcomed offer to become bloc’s first associate member, no one seems to know what that means

Mark Carney received a rapturous reception in the European parliament when he gave his speech on Thursday welcoming a proposal for Canada to become the EU’s first-ever associate member.

Politicians queued to shake his hand and take selfies. One described the speech as a historic moment. “Europe has extended a hand, and Canada has taken it,” said the German Green MEP Terry Reintke, who borrowed a Canadian ice hockey shirt for the occasion.

Continue reading...

items.title: IS member sentenced to 20 years in prison for role in 2021 Kabul airport bombing
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
Mohammad Sharifullah, 28, was convicted of aiding the terrorist group that took credit for the suicide bombing

An Islamic State group member was sentenced on Wednesday to 20 years in prison for aiding the terrorist organization that took credit for a suicide bombing that killed 13 US service members and about 160 Afghans at the Kabul airport five years ago during the US military’s chaotic withdrawal from the country.

A federal jury in Virginia had convicted Mohammad Sharifullah in April of providing material support to the IS affiliate known as Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP). But jurors could not agree whether he bore some responsibility for the airport bombing on 26 August 2021.

Continue reading...

      </article>

Cartoon: America’s AI-safety debate

items.title: Business
Markets are waking up to the rich world’s reckless borrowing
items.content:
<article>

items.title: Climate crisis probably weakened glacier that caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, first study finds
items.author: Damien Gayle
items.content:
Scientists say global heating was a destabilising factor in collapse of 200,000 sq metre glacier in August

Climate breakdown probably weakened the glacier that collapsed causing catastrophic floods and killing over a thousand people in Nepal and Tibet last month, the first scientific study of the disaster has found.

Researchers identified unusually warm conditions before the glacier’s collapse, which sent an avalanche of 110m cubic metres (3.885bn cu ft) of snow and ice into the valley below. This triggered flash floods on an almost unprecedented scale, hitting communities downstream without warning.
